html:
The Polans were a West Slavic tribe of the lowlands around Gniezno and Poznań, in what is now western Poland. The map shows them in 700, though written sources only mention them from about 1000.

Their name means "people of the open fields", and it gave Poland its name. Their ruling family, the Piasts, built a ring of wooden strongholds and brought neighbouring tribes under their rule in the 900s. In 966 Duke Mieszko I was baptised, an event remembered as the Baptism of Poland, and his state became Poland. Like other Early Slavs, they had lived as farmers in small villages before this.
